representations.text: Across March 30–April 12, all 14 days were complete and broadly stable versus the preceding 28 days. Mean sleep was 470.6 versus 470.3 minutes, with starts around 22:49 and waking consistently at 07:00; no sustained shortening occurred. Weekend sleep averaged 468.3 versus 471.6 weekday minutes, reversing the baseline’s small weekend advantage. Steps averaged 8,008 versus 8,039, while active minutes increased modestly from 55.2 to 57.8, consistently starting at 21:00. Low movement averaged 452.4 versus 449.7 minutes, distributed across ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Resting heart rate stayed within 55–57 bpm, averaging 55.9 versus 56.2. RMSSD averaged 40 ms in both periods, with a narrower current range of 28–52 versus 26–54; weekday variability remained greater than weekend variability. Activity versus next-wake-date sleep and heart rate versus RMSSD showed weak relationships. The baseline inverse steps–active-minutes association weakened substantially.

With complete observations, March 30–April 12 sleep averaged 440.6 versus 470.5 baseline minutes, but the change was concentrated late. Sleep initially lasted 474–485 minutes; April 7–12 brought six consecutive nights of 385–392 minutes, approximately 82 minutes below baseline, without recovery. Starts shifted from roughly 22:49 at baseline to 00:08–00:15, while waking remained 07:00, spanning weekdays and weekends. Activity changed from 50–60 minutes starting at 21:00 to six continuous 90-minute bouts at 20:30–22:00 and eight 45-minute bouts at 17:30–18:15; the mean rose from 55.6 to 64.3 minutes. Both schedules preceded short and longer sleep, with little aligned association across 13 pairs (r=-0.07). Steps averaged 8,088 versus 7,947; weekdays exceeded weekends, whose counts rose between weekends. Low movement remained near 449 versus 448 minutes in interrupted daytime bouts. Resting heart rate and RMSSD remained close to baseline: 56.4 versus 55.9 bpm and 45.7 versus 45.0 ms.

Complete March 30–April 12 records show interrupted sleep shortening: six isolated nights ending March 31 and April 2, 4, 8, 10 and 12 lasted 385–392 minutes versus the 470.5-minute baseline. Each followed a continuous 90-minute activity bout at 20:30–22:00, with sleep starting 00:08–00:15 and waking at 07:00. After the first five short nights, sleep returned the next night to 474–485 minutes; the final night has no observed follow-up. Across 13 aligned pairs, eight 45-minute bouts at 17:30–18:15 preceded longer sleep, producing a strong inverse duration association (r=-0.996), absent at baseline; this does not establish causation. The pattern crossed weekdays and weekends. Mean sleep fell to 440.6 minutes; active minutes rose from 55.6 to 64.3. Steps averaged 8,088 versus 7,947, with higher weekday counts. Low movement remained near 449 versus 448 minutes in interrupted bouts. Heart rate and RMSSD stayed near baseline: 56.4 versus 55.9 bpm and 45.7 versus 45.0 ms.

Steps increased abruptly on March 30 and stayed elevated throughout all 14 complete days: 7,927/day versus the preceding 28-day mean of 2,818, a rise of 5,109 (+181%). Every current day had 7,636–8,320 steps, exceeding the baseline maximum of 3,023. Weekday counts declined modestly within the window but remained elevated; weekends averaged 8,126 versus 7,847 on weekdays, compared with nearly identical baseline groups. Active minutes remained near baseline, 55.3 versus 56.2, in continuous bouts starting at 21:00; weekends decreased from 57.3 to 52.5 minutes despite higher steps. Steps and active minutes had little current association. Low movement fell slightly from 450.7 to 446.7 minutes, still comprising ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Sleep remained stable at 469.1 versus 470.8 minutes, starting around 22:51 and ending at 07:00. Resting heart rate averaged 55.9 versus 56.2 bpm and RMSSD 45.0 versus 44.9 ms. Activity versus next-wake-date sleep was weakly associated; heart rate and RMSSD were uncorrelated.
